topic: Gravity gate latch: why a gate locks itself when you push it shut. The catch on the post has a ramp that lifts the bar, gravity drops the bar into the notch, and the notch's straight wall stops it from coming out
title: How a Gate Locks Itself 🔒
principle: A gravity gate latch has a bar hung on a pin on the gate and a catch on the post; as the gate closes, the end of the bar meets the catch's inclined face and rides up it, then past the top it falls back by its own weight into a notch, whose near-vertical wall stops the bar when the gate is pulled, so the gate stays shut until someone lifts the bar above the catch.

firstComment:
Answer: gravity 🔧

A gravity latch has two parts: a steel bar that hangs on a pin on the gate, and a catch on the post.

As the gate closes, the end of the bar meets the catch's sloped ramp and rides up it. Past the top, the bar falls back down by its own weight into a notch. No spring needed.

Now try to pull the gate open: the bar hits the notch's straight wall and can't ride out, so the gate stays shut. To open it, lift the bar above the catch and swing the gate.

(Simplified 3D model, slowed down. Real latches differ in shape: on some, the ramp and notch are on the bar and the catch is a simple pin.)

Sources:
US Patent 858,866, Gate-latch (1907) (the keeper on the fence post presents an inclined face to the latch, which rides over it as the gate is closing and then drops over the keeper): https://patents.google.com/patent/US858866A/en
US Patent 2,671,683, Gate latch (a gravity-actuated gate latch: the striker hits the inclined surface and lifts the latch as the gate is closed, then gravity makes the latch fall back so the striker is locked in a notch with a vertical wall): https://patents.google.com/patent/US2671683
US Patent 413,193, Self-closing gate (the latch is lifted above the gravity catch before the gate opens): https://patents.google.com/patent/US413193
altText: 3D animation of a wooden garden gate with a steel gravity latch, with a voiceover. Under the question How does it lock itself? a red circle marks the steel catch on the gate post. An arrow pushes the gate shut, the steel bar slides up the catch and drops in with a click. Then a wide view with no latch: the gate is pushed shut and bounces back open. The latch fades back in and the parts are named: bar, pin, catch, ramp. From the side, slowly: 1, the ramp lifts the bar as the gate closes. 2, gravity drops it into the notch, click. 3, an arrow pulls the gate open, but the bar hits the flat wall of the notch: locked. The payoff reads A ramp to get in, a wall to stop it. Then an arrow lifts the bar's knob, the gate swings open and a follow line appears before the video loops.
